title: Lester's style on alto at the time; crazy about Bix, Frankie and Benny Goodman
summary: The band had a stock of The Stampede with Lester soloing on alto; his sound was already much as later and he admired Bix, Trumbauer and Goodman.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Bix Beiderbecke: hearing, copying and remembering him

blocks.x: Only in the band.
Only in the band. I never heard none of his records too much. Until later, after he came back from Europe.
He did that record called "The Stampede." Did you hear that one?
Yeah, sure. We used to play that.
How do you mean, you used to play that?
We used to play that... We had a stock on it.
The Willis Young band had a stock on it?
Yeah. There was a stock arrangement out on it then.
Did Lester take a solo on that?
Yeah. But he was playing alto.
What his solo style like at that time? You say he'd been listening to Trumbauer and...
Just about like it is now.
At that time?
Yeah, he would sound like that... See, he always had a small tone for a tenor. You noticed that.
But he was playing alto at that time.
He was playing alto. But we're getting
Phillips - 58
back to the tenor players, you know what I mean...?
Well, any influences on him is good... I mean, he listened to Beiderbecke, too, right?
Oh yeah. He was crazy about Bix.
He was crazy about Beiderbecke?
Oh yeah. Crazy about Frankie and crazy about Benny Goodman. Because Benny Goodman at that time was playing clarinet like he is now! So they used to make...
So you heard the Pollack records with Benny Goodman, is that it?
Yeah. When Benny was playing with Pollack. Then they used to...
